channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Davi Alcolumbre deve enviar indicação de Messias à CCJ nesta quinta e destravar sabatina ao STF
item.description: Senate President Davi Alcolumbre (União-AP) is expected to submit on Thursday (9) to the Constitution and Justice Committee (CCJ) President Lula’s nomination of Jorge Messias to the STF, after a four-month delay. The move should clear the way for Messias’ confirmation hearing at the Supreme Federal Court.

item.title: Indicado ao STF, Messias será sabatinado no Senado em 29 de abril
item.description: Union Advocate-General Jorge Messias, nominated by Lula for the STF, will be questioned by the Senate’s Constitution and Justice Committee on April 29. The hearing, lasting up to eight hours, will allow all 81 senators to ask questions, followed by secret votes in the committee and plenary, requiring an absolute majority of 41 votes for approval. The nomination, settled since November, was finalized after political negotiations, with Senator Rodrigo Pacheco (PSB-MG) playing a key role in overcoming Senate resistance.

item.title: Dino pede vista e interrompe julgamento sobre eleições no Rio
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Flávio Dino requested additional time (vista) to review the case determining how the new governor of Rio de Janeiro will be chosen following Cláudio Castro's (PL) departure from office. The hearing, which began on Wednesday, April 8, resumed on Thursday, April 9, but was suspended to allow further analysis.

item.title: Lula sanciona leis para fortalecer combate à violência contra mulheres
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva signed three laws to strengthen the fight against violence against women, including electronic monitoring of aggressors, expansion of protective measures, and increased penalties for femicide. The measures aim to provide greater protection to victims and greater accountability for perpetrators.

item.title: Moraes veta pedido de Lindbergh para que Moro fosse investigado por fala
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes denied a request by federal deputy Lindbergh Farias (PT-RJ) to investigate Senator Sergio Moro (PL-PR) over statements questioning the legitimacy of the 2022 elections. The request followed Moro's claims that electronic voting machines could have been fraudulent, but Moraes found insufficient grounds to open an inquiry. The decision underscores the STF's stance on protecting political speech, even when controversial, under freedom of expression.

item.title: Janja corrige Lula durante sanção de leis de proteção à mulher
item.description: First Lady Janja Lula da Silva corrected President Lula during a speech at the Planalto Palace, pointing out that the 5,000 arrests for gender-based violence were of men, not people in general. Lula repeated the corrected statement. The incident occurs amid a history of controversial remarks by the president, including statements deemed misogynistic, and reflects a media strategy by Secom that increased his exposure and risk of gaffes.

item.title: Governo estuda liberar R$ 7 bi do FGTS para endividados, mas Caixa não confirma valor
item.description: The government is studying the release of R$ 7 billion from the FGTS that was not withdrawn by workers due to an incomplete disbursement in the 2025 birthday-savings withdrawals, according to the Ministry of Labor. Caixa Econômica Federal did not confirm the amount, stating it strictly follows legislation and the FGTS Curatorial Board’s directives. Approximately 10 million workers could benefit from the release of this remaining amount.

item.title: André Mendonça vai decidir se manda Congresso ressuscitar PL da Dosimetria
item.description: Supreme Court Justice André Mendonça has been assigned as rapporteur in a lawsuit filed by ASFAV seeking to compel the National Congress to reconsider presidential vetoes on the Dosimetry Bill. Congress President Davi Alcolumbre indicated plans to meet with Chamber President Hugo Motta to schedule a vote on overturning Lula’s full veto of the bill, which was approved by the Senate in December. The suit alleges legislative omission by lawmakers regarding the radiation dosimetry measure.

item.title: Aliados de Lula buscam momento ideal para começar a desgastar Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Lula’s allies say they are waiting for the right moment to begin damaging Flávio Bolsonaro’s image, the PL’s presidential candidate, despite his stronger-than-expected polling performance. They believe that since over half of voters could still change their minds, timing the attack strategically is crucial to prevent a recovery by the opposition. With Lula and Flávio technically tied in recent polls, the ruling coalition aims to weaken the rival carefully to avoid a repeat of the emotionally charged 2022 election outcome.

item.title: “É mais fácil tirar voto do Flávio que do Lula”, afirma Kassab
item.description: Gilberto Kassab, president of the PSD, stated that it is easier to take votes from Flávio Bolsonaro than from Lula due to the latter's stronger voter loyalty and the fluidity of the right-wing electorate, often driven by opposition to the other side. He positioned Goiás Governor Ronaldo Caiado as a competitive alternative to attract conservatives dissatisfied with polarization, emphasizing that the 2026 electoral landscape is still forming and depends on the consolidation of candidacies and alliances.

item.title: Mendonça se preocupa com “deslegitimação” do TSE
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes expressed concern over the potential delegitimization of the Superior Electoral Court (TSE) amid a conflict between the two courts regarding the rules for Rio de Janeiro's supplementary gubernatorial election. The dispute centers on whether the interim mandate should be decided by direct popular vote or indirect vote by the state Legislative Assembly. The issue is currently under review by the Supreme Court, which is assessing the constitutionality of existing electoral rules.

item.title: Eleição e bolso: o conceito de 'affordability' que explica por que bons números da economia não garantem votos; ouça 'O Assunto'
item.description: Despite positive macroeconomic indicators in Brazil, many citizens do not feel an improvement in their quality of life due to the concept of 'affordability,' which measures the real ability to cope with the cost of living. Qualitative research identifies three key factors: excessive indebtedness (overdraft, credit cards, consigned loans), consumption frustration (inability to access well-being-associated goods like 'picanha e cerveja'), and hidden spending on online betting (bets), which silently erode household income without clear awareness.

item.title: Lula nomeia 1ª mulher para comandar agência de assistência rural
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva appointed agronomist engineer Loroana Santana as the first woman to lead Anater, the National Agency for Technical Assistance and Rural Extension, linked to the Ministry of Agrarian Development and Family Farming. The appointment, published in the Official Gazette on April 9, 2026, also highlights Fernanda Machiaveli's historic role as the first woman to head the ministry.

item.title: CCJ marca sabatina de Messias para 29 de abril, e relator adianta voto favorável
item.description: The Senate's Constitution and Justice Committee (CCJ) has scheduled the hearing for Jorge Messias, President Lula's nominee for the Supreme Federal Court (STF), for April 29, with the rapporteur already indicating a favorable vote. On the same date, the CCJ and the plenary are expected to vote on the nomination, as outlined by the committee's president. This accelerates the process of filling the vacancy on Brazil's highest court.

item.title: O que o Planalto espera da sabatina de Messias
item.description: Planalto officials are confident that Jorge Messias, Lula’s nominee to the STF, will be approved by the Senate’s CCJ in a hearing scheduled for April 29. They believe he has sufficient support to pass both the committee and the full plenary vote, potentially exceeding Flávio Dino’s 47 votes in his hearing. This optimism is bolstered by Senate President Davi Alcolumbre’s signal not to delay the process and the anticipated reduction in opposition if Rodrigo Pacheco runs for governor of Minas Gerais.

item.title: Alcolumbre marca sabatina de Jorge Messias na CCJ do Senado
item.description: Senate President Davi Alcolumbre has scheduled the confirmation hearing for Jorge Messias before the Constitution and Justice Committee on April 29, with rapporteur Weverton Rocha already indicating a favorable vote. The nomination of the current Attorney General of the Union to the Supreme Federal Court, made by Lula after a four-month vacancy, will proceed to a secret plenary vote the same day, requiring at least 41 votes for approval. Despite lacking initial vote guarantees, the government maintained its strategy to advance the process to avoid proximity with the electoral calendar, and historically the Senate rarely rejects Supreme Court nominees.

item.title: CCJ do Senado marca para 29/4 sabatina de Messias, indicado ao STF
item.description: The hearing for Jorge Messias, nominated to the STF by President Lula, is scheduled for April 29 in the Senate’s CCJ, with the report reading set for April 15. The nomination was submitted to the Senate on April 1, 2026, after delays due to political wear, as Senate President Davi Alcolumbre had preferred Senator Rodrigo Pacheco for the vacancy. Messias, current Attorney General of the Union, has dined with senators and Zanin to secure support for his approval.

item.title: Lula mantém urgência para projeto do fim da escala 6×1 após ruído com Motta
item.description: President Lula reaffirmed the urgency of the bill to end the 6×1 work schedule, contradicting an premature statement by PT Chamber leader Pedro Uczai, who had suggested abandoning the urgency regime. The government decided to maintain the original strategy and will send the bill this week, despite the disagreement with Chamber President Hugo Motta, who favors processing the matter through a constitutional amendment (PEC).

item.title: Ex-secretário de Bolsonaro atua na defesa de Vorcaro por R$ 3,8 milhões
item.description: Fabio Wajngarten, former communications secretary under Jair Bolsonaro, is defending former banker Daniel Vorcaro through his firm WF Comunicação, which received R$ 3.8 million from Banco Master in 2025. Wajngarten stated he joined Vorcaro’s defense team in the first half of 2025 via the banker’s lawyers and claims he is no longer a politically exposed person. The case also reveals multi-million-dollar payments to law firms tied to figures like Michel Temer, ACM Neto, and STF ministers, including R$ 80 million to the firm of Alexandre de Moraes’ wife.

item.title: Messias no STF: relator diz que apresentará relatório favorável ao indicado de Lula em 15 de abril
item.description: Senator Weverton Rocha (PDT-MA), rapporteur for Jorge Messias' STF nomination, said he will present a favorable report in the CCJ on April 15. Messias' confirmation hearing is set for April 29, after the government delivered the official nomination on April 1, ending a standoff with the Senate. He needs at least 41 secret votes in the plenary to be approved.

item.title: Após crítica de Lula, Petrobras anula leilão e devolve valores do gás
item.description: Petrobras has canceled the March 31 auction of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) and will refund overcharged amounts following criticism from President Lula, who called the auction 'cretinism' and 'banditry'. The decision, based on economic and risk analyses, accounts for the Middle East conflict and regulatory input from ANP and Senacon. The company is also evaluating adherence to a government subsidy program for imported LPG to compensate consumers.

item.title: Moraes rejeita pedido de Lindbergh para investigar Moro
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes rejected a request by Congressman Lindbergh Farias (PT-RJ) to investigate Senator Sergio Moro (PL-PR) over remarks questioning the legitimacy of the 2022 elections. Moraes ruled that only the Attorney General's Office has standing to initiate criminal proceedings against lawmakers, citing the constitutional monopoly on public criminal action. The PGR had previously opposed the request and asked for its withdrawal.

item.title: Zema descarta ser vice de Flávio Bolsonaro e reafirma candidatura própria à Presidência
item.description: Romeu Zema ruled out being Flávio Bolsonaro's running mate and reaffirmed his own presidential bid, stating no formal invitation was ever made. He criticized Supreme Court justices Alexandre de Moraes and Dias Toffoli, calling their actions criminal, and proposed a penal aggravant for public officials who betray the nation. Zema also advocated for administrative reform, reducing the number of ministries, and a new pension reform with automatic adjustments tied to life expectancy.

item.title: Silveira cobra que Axia atue na reestruturação do setor nuclear brasileiro
item.description: Mines and Energy Minister Alexandre Silveira publicly urged Ivan Monteiro, president of Axia Energy (formerly Eletrobras), to participate in restructuring Brazil's nuclear sector during Latam Energy Week 2026. He reiterated his support for completing Angra 3 and defended nuclear energy as a future strategic asset, stressing the government's partnership with Axia as a shareholder in Eletronuclear.

item.title: Alcolumbre envia à CCJ indicação de Messias ao STF, e Weverton é escolhido relator
item.description: Senate President Davi Alcolumbre forwarded President Lula's message nominating Attorney General Jorge Messias to the STF to the CCJ. Senator Weverton Rocha (PDT-MA) was appointed as rapporteur for the nomination in the committee.

item.title: Gilmar Mendes diz que ouviu de diretor da PF que '32 ou 34 parlamentares da Alerj recebem mesada do jogo do bicho'
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Gilmar Mendes stated he heard from the Federal Police Director General that 32 or 34 members of the Rio de Janeiro State Legislature (Alerj) receive a 'stipend' from the illegal gambling game 'jogo do bicho', during a session discussing the interim election in the state. The proceedings were suspended after Minister Flávio Dino requested a view, urging to await the TSE’s ruling on former Governor Cláudio Castro. Conversely, Minister André Mendonça urged an early vote in favor of indirect elections, citing governance instability due to the lingering interim governor arrangement.

item.title: A ira dos ambientalistas com consumo de carne de paca por Lula e Janja
item.description: The Easter lunch of President Lula and First Lady Janja, featuring paca meat from an Ibama-authorized breeding facility, sparked criticism from environmental activists like Luisa Mell and the NGO Fórum Animal, who argue that public figures consuming wild animals — even legally — normalizes practices tied to illegal hunting and threatens biodiversity. Janja defended the meal as a legal gift from an authorized producer, reiterating her animal welfare stance, but experts warn that such visibility undermines conservation campaigns and may encourage illegal wildlife trade targeting species like pacas, tapirs, caimans, and turtles.

item.title: Galípolo não seguiu o combinado com Lula?
item.description: Central Bank President Gabriel Galípolo did not follow the strategy agreed upon with President Lula to blame Roberto Campos Neto, the former BC head appointed by Bolsonaro, for the Banco Master scandal. The agreement was made during a meeting at the Planalto Palace in March, but Galípolo chose not to assign blame to Neto, according to O Globo. This divergence suggests potential tension in coordination between the government and the monetary authority.

item.title: Alcolumbre destrava indicação de Messias, e sabatina é marcada para 29 de abril
item.description: Senate President Davi Alcolumbre has unblocked the nomination of Jorge Messias to the Supreme Court, scheduling the confirmation hearing for April 29. The report reading will take place on April 15, over four months after the nomination was first announced. The progress follows government-led political outreach, including a dinner with senators and visible support from Justice Cristiano Zanin.

item.title: Mendonça e Cármen Lúcia afirmam que julgamento no STF sobre eleição no Rio deslegitima TSE
item.description: STF Ministers André Mendonça and Cármen Lúcia criticized the TSE's analysis of the Rio de Janeiro election, claiming the STF's judgment illegitimizes the Superior Electoral Court by reviewing the case before the TSE's ruling on Cláudio Castro's conviction was published. They argue the STF is prematurely asserting jurisdiction over matters still under the TSE's authority, creating institutional conflict and uncertainty.

item.title: Alcolumbre envia indicação de Messias à CCJ e destrava análise; Weverton é definido relator e sabatina será no dia 29
item.description: Senate President Davi Alcolumbre forwarded the nomination of Attorney General Jorge Messias to the CCJ, unlocking its analysis for the STF. Senator Weverton Rocha (PDT-MA) was appointed rapporteur, with the hearing set for the 29th. Approval requires at least 41 votes in the Senate plenary, and voting will be secret in both the CCJ and plenary.

item.title: Dino pede vistas em julgamento sobre eleições no RJ; Mendonça antecipa voto
item.description: Justice Flávio Dino requested a view in the STF's judgment on indirect elections in Rio de Janeiro, while André Mendonça anticipated his vote. The case involves two actions determining whether Rio's elections will be indirect (by state deputies) or direct (by popular vote), after a preliminary injunction by Justice Cristiano Zanin suspended the indirect process.

item.title: Líder do PT vê recado de Lula à base ao evitar cravar candidatura à reeleição
item.description: The leader of the PT in the Chamber of Deputies, Pedro Uczai, stated that Lula's declaration that he has not yet decided whether to run for re-election is a calculated strategy to mobilize the party's base and stimulate grassroots engagement, avoiding premature arrogance. According to him, the president is not backing down from candidacy but is respecting internal party processes, such as conventions, and believes victory will depend on political organization, not just government action. Uczai said he has no doubt Lula will be the candidate and sees time to consolidate the government's project despite current low societal mobilization.

item.title: Lula endurece regras em novo pacote contra violência à mulher
item.description: President Lula signed three bills to combat violence against women, including electronic ankle monitors for aggressors, the criminalization of 'vicarious crime' (harming third parties to traumatize women), and the establishment of a National Day for the Protection and Combat of Violence Against Indigenous Women. He stressed that while strict laws are necessary, they alone cannot solve the problem without prevention, criticized the lack of digital regulation and online platforms for enabling violence, and noted that many victims remain silent due to lack of trusted support.

item.title: Flávio Dino pede vista e adia decisão sobre eleições para governador-tampão no RJ
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Flávio Dino requested a view of the cases concerning the election for interim governor of Rio de Janeiro, postponing the decision. The position will govern the state until the end of 2026 following the current governor's departure. The request for a view temporarily halts the judgment at the STF.

item.title: Dino pede vista de julgamento que vai decidir sobre eleição para governo do Rio de Janeiro
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Flávio Dino requested a view in the judgment determining whether the Rio de Janeiro gubernatorial election will be direct or indirect following the resignation and cassation of Governor Cláudio Castro. He argued that the court must await the publication of the TSE’s ruling that cassated Castro’s mandate before proceeding. In the meantime, he advocates that the president of the Rio de Janeiro Court of Justice remain in office. Justices Cristiano Zanin and Luiz Fux have already voted: Zanin favors direct popular vote, while Fux supports an indirect election by the state legislature.

item.title: Motta deve escantear medida de Lula para acelerar fim da escala 6×1
item.description: House Speaker Hugo Motta is expected to prioritize the existing PEC to end the 6×1 work schedule, rather than accept President Lula’s push for an urgent bill on the same issue. Motta’s allies say he will resist Executive interference in the legislative agenda, relying on internal rules that allow PECs to proceed even if the floor agenda is locked. The PEC is set for a vote in the CCJ in the last week of April before moving to a special committee and the plenary.

item.title: Pode ser injusto, mas a maior marca do governo Lula 3 é o caso Master
item.description: Lula's third government is suffering declining popularity due to the Banco Master scandal, with the president attempting to shift blame to the right despite involvement of his allies. The crisis deepens with revelations that Alexandre de Moraes' wife received R$ 80 million from the bank, undermining his anti-Bolsonaro hero image and directly damaging public perception of the administration.

item.title: Dino pede vista e adia julgamento sobre eleição de mandato-tampão no Rio
item.description: Minister Flávio Dino requested a view in the STF judgment on how to elect the temporary governor of Rio de Janeiro following Cláudio Castro's resignation, postponing his vote until the TSE publishes its ruling on Castro's case. The court was tied 1-1, with Cristiano Zanin supporting direct elections and Luiz Fux favoring indirect ones, while André Mendonça urged an early vote due to the vacancy's urgency.

item.title: Justiça do DF condena Gayer por ofensa misógina contra Gleisi
item.description: The Federal District Court of Justice condemned Deputy Gustavo Gayer (PL-GO) to pay a BRL 20,000 indemnity for misogynistic offenses against Gleisi Hoffmann, and ordered a public retraction on social media within ten days. The ruling overturned a first-instance decision, stating Gayer's language was vulgar, sexualized, and devoid of political content. Gleisi and Lindbergh Farias celebrated the decision as a clear message against sexism and political violence.

item.title: Renan Santos admite uso de cogumelos alucinógenos
item.description: Renan Santos, a presidential pre-candidate from the Missão party, admitted to consuming hallucinogenic mushrooms (Psilocybe cubensis) on three occasions, based on leaked Instagram messages from April 2024 to October 2025. He downplayed the impact, stating the use was occasional and in microdoses, and denied it constituted drug trafficking financing, despite his main platform being the fight against narcotics. A criminal complaint filed with the MPF-DF by student Ian Bartholo Lukas Coelho may lead to legal consequences affecting his eligibility.

item.title: Saída antecipada de Cármen Lúcia pegou até ministros da corte de surpresa
item.description: The early departure of Minister Cármen Lúcia from the presidency of the Superior Electoral Court (TSE) surprised even other justices, who were not informed in advance of her decision. The move occurred earlier than expected and raised concerns about internal transparency within the body responsible for overseeing elections in Brazil.

item.title: STF retoma julgamento que vai decidir sobre eleição para governo do Rio de Janeiro
item.description: The Brazilian Supreme Court resumed its trial to determine whether the Rio de Janeiro gubernatorial election will be direct (popular vote) or indirect (decided by state legislators), following the resignation and removal of Claudio Castro. Minister Cristiano Zanin voted for direct election, while Luiz Fux supported indirect voting with secret ballot. Justices also agreed on a 24-hour incompatibility period for candidates to resign from current offices.

item.title: Tarcísio aciona Rodrigo Garcia e Vinholi para conter desgaste com prefeitos
item.description: Governor Tarcísio de Freitas has appointed former governor Rodrigo Garcia and former regional development secretary Marco Vinholi to mend relations with interior São Paulo mayors, amid complaints of poor communication and reduced state funding transfers. Despite the strain, mayors acknowledge Tarcísio remains electorally competitive due to Bolsonarist support, even without direct reliance on municipal governments.

item.title: Kassab projeta PSD forte no RJ e exalta Paes: ‘Sem acusações de corrupção’
item.description: Gilberto Kassab, national president of the PSD, projected strong party performance in Rio de Janeiro for the 2026 elections, highlighting Eduardo Paes as a competitive and experienced candidate free from personal corruption allegations. He also endorsed Ronaldo Caiado (União Brasil) as a future presidential candidate and emphasized the PSD's Rio strategy will focus on grassroots 'body-to-body' campaigning, despite reduced reliance on physical rallies due to social media.

item.title: Lula: se não obrigar plataformas a cuidarem dos limites internet, não é pai que vai conseguir
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva advocated for social media regulation, urging platforms to be required to control harmful content reaching adolescents, stressing that responsibility cannot fall solely on parents. He made the remarks while signing laws to combat violence against women, linking digital regulation to the protection of vulnerable groups.

item.title: Entre aplausos e vaias, episódio com Flávio revela tom da disputa presidencial
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro's appearance at the Chamber of Deputies during the launch of Soraya Santos' candidacy for the TCU revealed the polarized climate expected in the 2026 presidential race. Greeted with both cheers and boos, he responded with gestures like a hand-formed heart while facing chants of 'my president' and criticisms over issues such as 'rachadinha', property purchases, and amnesty. According to columnist Mauro Paulino, this episode directly reflects the confrontational environment candidates will face, with potential for tension escalation—but not violence—and public reaction will be decisive in shaping voter perception.

item.title: PT prepara atos pelo fim da escala 6 x 1 no 1º de Maio
item.description: The PT is preparing a national mobilization for May Day, with events in all 27 states, marches, plenaries, and a digital campaign, centered on ending the 6x1 work schedule. The party will send an urgency bill to Congress to abolish the schedule, coordinated with unions and social movements, as part of its 2026 electoral strategy.

item.title: Pesquisa Real Time Big Data mostra Lula perdendo fôlego em reduto histórico do PT
item.description: A Real Time Big Data poll shows President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s voting intention in Pernambuco has dropped to 56%, about ten points below his 2022 performance, raising concerns for his re-election campaign as the Northeast remains his main electoral base. The decline signals organized right-wing advances in the region, while the PT seeks to expand into traditional opposition strongholds like São Paulo, reflecting a more balanced and nationalized territorial contest ahead of the 2026 elections.

item.title: TSE retomará julgamento de ex-governador de Roraima na próxima 3ª
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) will resume the trial of former Roraima governor Antonio Denarium (Republicans) on Tuesday, April 14, 2026, over allegations of abuse of political and economic power in the 2022 elections, including the use of public funds in social programs like 'Cesta da Família' and 'Morar Melhor' to boost his re-election. The trial was suspended in November 2025 after a vista request by Minister Nunes Marques and now has two votes already favoring his removal from office. The case was filed by the coalition 'Roraima Muito Melhor', led by the MDB party and Teresa Surita, who received 41.14% of the vote in 2022.
